scores.visual_critic_note: Deliberate Paul Tol palette and split-violin small-multiples design support a clear visual argument about decadal warming, but Singapore's near-zero amplitude collapses its row into illegible horizontal dashes and the small cell size limits the form's expressiveness.
scores.encoding_integrity_note: Violin widths use linear density-to-width mapping (correct for KDE plots), y-scale domain is fully data-driven via d3.extent, Silverman bandwidth is properly computed, and global maxDensity normalization enables honest cross-cell comparison — minor robustness concern: removing a high-density record (e.g. Singapore) would rescale all other violins due to shared maxDensity.
scores.stress_test_note: No brush/zoom/transitions present; pointer events API unifies mouse-touch correctly; pointerenter DOM work (selectAll rows/labels) is once-per-entry not per-frame, so no update storm; static pre-computed data eliminates stale closure risk entirely.
scores.cognitive_load_note: 72-cell grid (6 cities × 12 months) reads as one conceptual unit with a two-color split-violin encoding, shared y-scale, and alternating row bands that together make the seasonal arc and latitude gradient scannable at a glance; cells are small but simple enough in shape that the pattern holds, and hover interaction surfaces exact stats without adding visual noise.

proposer: Changed median lines from white (`#fff`) to dark (`#222`) with a white drop-shadow for contrast. This addresses both audit callouts: "median legend line nearly invisible on the light background" (visual_critic) and "median lines are hard to see at the small cell size" (cognitive_load).
